name: Textured PEI (powder-coated spring steel)
summary: The modern default build surface: powder-coated polyetherimide on flexible spring steel. Grips hot, releases cold, needs no adhesives for most materials, and leaves a uniform textured finish. Example entry pending Phase D research.
surface_makeup: Polyetherimide (PEI) powder coating fused onto a spring-steel sheet

filament_compatibility.notes: Wash with dish soap if adhesion drops — skin oils are the usual culprit
Texture prevents the PEI-fusing problem smooth sheets have with PETG

filament_compatibility.adhesion_aid: none or thin glue stick on large flats
filament_compatibility.notes: Enclosure matters more than the plate for ASA adhesion

preparation: First use and periodically: wash with warm water and unscented dish soap, dry with a clean paper towel. Avoid touching the print area. IPA between prints removes light residue but eventually smears oils — soap wash beats IPA.
cleaning: Routine: 91%+ IPA wipe when cold. Deep: dish-soap scrub. Never scrape with metal on the coating; acetone is unnecessary and can degrade some coatings.
model_removal: Let the plate cool below ~40 °C, then flex the sheet — prints pop free. Cold-release is the design feature; prying hot defeats it.
stuck_print_recovery: Put the plate (with print) in a freezer for 10–15 minutes, then flex. For thin flat prints, flex progressively from a corner. As a last resort slide a thin plastic spatula under an edge — never metal blades on the coating.
lifespan_notes: Coating wears glossy in high-use zones over months-to-years; adhesion loss that soap washing doesn't fix indicates wear. Sheets can be re-powder-coated by some vendors or replaced.
additional_notes: TPU can bond aggressively if printed too hot on fresh coating — first candidate for a 'usable-with-prep' rating once TPU entry exists.

sources: EXAMPLE ENTRY — verify manufacturers, temps, and care guidance in Phase D
